articles.title: 'Population up in 40 China-border villages': Amit Shah reaches out to Arunachal amid dam protests
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday reached out to Arunachal Pradesh amid protests over a proposed dam project, saying the population in 40
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday reached out to Arunachal Pradesh amid protests over a proposed dam project, saying the population in 40 villages bordering China has increased and migration has stopped, citing improved employment, healthcare and other facilities. He made the remarks at a cooperative conference in the state, where he also announced development projects under the Centre’s Vibrant Villages Programme.Shah said the Centre has directed the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) to procure produce from local cooperatives in border villages instead of sourcing it from cities, strengthening ties between residents and security forces.“I reviewed this yesterday. I am pleased that people have begun returning to all 40 villages (bordering with China), the population there has increased, and migration has stopped. Electricity, employment, and health facilities have been discussed. Water has also been delivered to the hilltops. The Home Ministry has strictly mandated that the ITBP and the Army should not procure their produce from Tezpur or Guwahati; they must be procured from villages and cooperatives,” news agency ANI quoted Shah as saying.“Women in Arunachal Pradesh are supplying dairy products, eggs, vegetables, millets and flour through their cooperatives, bringing prosperity to rural households and transforming local agriculture and strengthening the relationship between villages and the army,” he added.He said employment, education, healthcare and the prosperity of every family should be the key priorities for Arunachal Pradesh's development. He urged cooperative institutions and women's self-help groups (SHGs) to work towards making the state self-reliant in essential food products.“Every cooperative institution and women Self-Help Groups (SHGs) should take up the challenge of making Arunachal Pradesh self-reliant in essential food products. Employment, education, healthcare and the prosperity of every family must be the four key priorities of Arunachal Pradesh's development,” Shah said.He also assured Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu and the deputy chief minister of the Centre's support for development projects, saying the government would open all avenues for the state's progress.“Yesterday, we discussed in detail all the steps of Arunachal's development for about three and a half to four hours, decided the roadmaps for the future, and made some decisions. Kiren Rijiju and I have taken note of things where the central government’s help is needed. I want to assure Pema Khandu and the deputy chief minister that the central government will open all avenues for the development of Arunachal without any delay. Mobile Medical Units were dispatched today to villages in 11 border districts under the Vibrant Village Programme,” he said.Shah also praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's decision to reframe border villages as the country's first villages rather than its last, saying they have the right to development.“Vibrant Village Programme was made for villages in border states. Earlier it was called the country’s last village; Narendra Modi changed the concept and awarded the title of the first village in the country. The biggest right to development is of the border villages of the country,” the Union minister said.Shah on Sunday launched 199 development projects worth Rs 110.95 crore under the Vibrant Villages Programme across 11 border districts of Arunachal Pradesh. He also unveiled the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047, a blueprint outlining the sector's development over the coming decades.Earlier on Saturday, Shah chaired a high-level review meeting in Itanagar to discuss law and order, internal security, border management and development in Arunachal Pradesh.He also reviewed border security and strategic infrastructure along Arunachal Pradesh's approximately 1,126-km international border with China, given its strategic sensitivity.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Phoenix man received a deed from his father in 2015, but its street address pointed to another property; four years later a company claimed the same land, and a 2026 appeals court upheld the invalidation of its competing deeds
articles.summary: A mistake in a property's street address can lead to years of legal disputes, particularly when competing deeds are recorded against the same land.
articles.body: A mistake in a property's street address can lead to years of legal disputes, particularly when competing deeds are recorded against the same land. In Phoenix, Arizona, a disagreement over a father's transfer of property to his son escalated into a lawsuit after a company claimed ownership of the same land and recorded its own deeds. The dispute eventually reached the Arizona Court of Appeals, which upheld a ruling invalidating the company's competing documents.In a November 19, 2026, memorandum decision available on Justia, the Arizona Court of Appeals, Division One, affirmed the lower court's judgment in Bonitas Casitas, LLC v. Olsen. The court found that the son's 2015 quitclaim deed remained presumptively valid despite an incorrect street address because it included an attached warranty deed containing the correct legal description of the Phoenix property. It also upheld the decision to remove the company's deeds from the county property records.How a mistake in the 2015 deed led to a property disputeThe case involved Robert Olsen, who received a quitclaim deed from his father in 2015 transferring ownership of a Phoenix property. Although the document listed the street address of a different property in Seligman, Arizona, it attached a deed containing the correct legal description of the Phoenix property. The error later became central to a dispute over who legally owned the Phoenix property.In 2019, Olsen's father executed another deed, this time transferring the Phoenix property to Bonitas Casitas LLC. The company subsequently claimed ownership based on that warranty deed, creating competing claims over the same land. Bonitas filed a lawsuit against Olsen in 2020, alleging that he had wrongfully recorded documents claiming an interest in the property. These included a special warranty deed transferring the Phoenix property from Olsen to the Robert Olsen Property Trust, as well as a deed of trust placing an encumbrance on the land.Olsen and the property trust filed counterclaims against Bonitas and Gregory Best, a business associate of the company's sole principal. They argued that Bonitas' 2019 warranty deed and a correction deed recorded by Best in 2020 were also wrongful. The correction deed attempted to change the legal description associated with the 2015 transaction, replacing the description of the Phoenix property with that of the Seligman property.Why the lower court invalidated the company's deedsThe dispute centred on whether Bonitas qualified as an owner or beneficial title holder of the Phoenix property when the competing deeds were recorded in 2019, a requirement for seeking remedies under Arizona Revised Statutes Section 33-420. In March 2023, the Maricopa County Superior Court granted summary judgment in favour of Olsen, dismissing Bonitas' claim for damages under Arizona law. It found that the company was not an owner or beneficial title holder of the Phoenix property when Olsen recorded his 2015 deed and therefore could not pursue that particular claim.The court also granted partial summary judgment on Olsen and the trust's counterclaim. It ordered the invalidation of Bonitas' 2019 warranty deed and Best's 2020 correction deed, clearing both documents from the property's title records. The litigation continued over other claims. In 2023, the property trust sold the Phoenix property to Tamarindo Investments LLC. The company later sought to replace the trust as a party in the proceedings so that the final judgment could also reflect its interest in the property.The Superior Court approved the substitution, dismissed the remaining unadjudicated claims and entered a final judgment formally declaring the two competing deeds invalid and void.Appeals court explains why the 2015 deed remained validBonitas and Best appealed, challenging the summary judgment rulings and the substitution of Tamarindo Investments. The Arizona Court of Appeals examined the state's property-recording law, particularly Arizona Revised Statutes Section 33-420. The provision allows an owner or beneficial title holder to seek remedies when false or fraudulent documents are wrongfully recorded against real estate.The appeals court noted that a recorded quitclaim deed is presumptively valid when it is properly signed, delivered and recorded. It also observed that the 2015 deed attached a deed containing the correct legal description of the Phoenix property, despite listing the wrong common street address.The court pointed out that the Maricopa County Recorder's Office had recognised the 2015 deed in the property's title history as a transfer from Olsen's father to his son. The Maricopa County Assessor had recognised Olsen's 2019 special warranty deed as superior to Bonitas' 2019 deed, while the City of Phoenix had cited Olsen as the title holder several times in 2018.Because the 2015 deed had not been challenged or invalidated, Olsen and subsequently the trust were the record owners when Bonitas and Best recorded their competing documents in 2019 and 2020. The court also explained that clearing a wrongfully recorded document under Section 33-420 is different from bringing a formal quiet title action to determine ownership of a property. Bonitas had not pursued the required quiet title proceedings.Ultimately, the appeals court found no error in the lower court's decision to invalidate the company's two deeds or allow Tamarindo to replace the trust in the case. It affirmed the judgment and granted Tamarindo reasonable appellate attorney fees and costs, subject to compliance with the applicable court rules.The decision is unpublished and non-precedential under Arizona Supreme Court Rule 111(c), meaning it generally cannot be cited as legal precedent except as permitted by the rule.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russian drone strike collapses apartment building in Kyiv region, 14 feared trapped
articles.summary: At least 14 people may be trapped under the rubble of a residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region after a Russian drone struck it on Sunday morning,
articles.body: At least 14 people may be trapped under the rubble of a residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region after a Russian drone struck it on Sunday morning, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Nine people have been evacuated from the damaged five-storey building, while emergency teams continue search and rescue operations. Two people, including a teenager, were injured, local officials said."Part of a five-storey apartment building has collapsed following a Russian drone attack. I thank our first responders for acting quickly: nine people have already been evacuated, and the fire has been contained," Zelenskyy said on X.Footage released by emergency services showed rescuers searching through a large pile of rubble. Some residents were helped out of the damaged building using ladders and a crane platform.The attack came amid continued drone strikes between Russia and Ukraine. In Russia, five people were injured in overnight Ukrainian drone attacks on the Krasnodar region, Russian media reported on Sunday.State news agency TASS, citing regional authorities, said four of the injured were in the village of Afipsky. The village is home to an oil refinery that has been repeatedly targeted by Ukrainian forces in recent months.Russian attacks deepen crisis in KyivThe latest attack comes as Kyiv faces increasingly frequent Russian strikes, which have worsened security conditions and disrupted daily life in the Ukrainian capital.Since September, Russia has stepped up attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas, targeting infrastructure, including power facilities, railway stations, roads and shopping centres.The deteriorating situation has also hit businesses, particularly restaurants and cafes, as residents avoid the city centre amid frequent air raid alerts.In September and October, Kyiv recorded 437 hours of air alerts. With sirens sounding for long periods, many residents have chosen to stay home rather than visit restaurants and other public spaces.Several hospitality businesses have shut down or suspended operations until the end of winter. Restaurant chain Gastro Family has closed two outlets in Kyiv and suspended operations at two others until April, its owner Olena Borysova told Reuters.Chornomorka, a seafood restaurant chain, has reported a roughly 20 per cent drop in customer visits compared with last year. The company has closed two restaurants in Kyiv and plans to relocate them to western Ukraine."It's not about earning or making any profit," the chain's development director Dmytro Kostrubin said. "The lucky one is the one who can break even."The crisis has also affected other restaurant groups. Pesto Cafe temporarily closed seven of its 20 restaurants in Kyiv and the surrounding region because of frequent air raids and worsening security conditions.According to Ukraine's National Restaurant Association, the country's restaurant sector employs around 150,000 people and generated about 248 billion hryvnias ($5 billion) in sales last year.Restaurant owners have tried to adapt by installing generators and water tanks to deal with power and water cuts. Some have also developed menus that can be prepared without electricity or running water.However, rising costs, staff shortages, curfews and falling consumer spending have made it increasingly difficult for businesses to remain operational.Annual inflation reached 11 per cent in October, putting further pressure on household budgets. Restaurant owners have reported that customers are spending less, often cutting out additional drinks and desserts.Borysova said the average order at her restaurants had fallen from three items to two as customers became more cautious about spending.You use AI every day. articles.title: UP polls: SP names four-member panel for seat-sharing talks with Congress from Monday
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress are set to hold a two-day meeting in New Delhi from Monday to discuss seat-sharing for the upcoming
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress are set to hold a two-day meeting in New Delhi from Monday to discuss seat-sharing for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, news agency ANI reported.The meeting will mark the first round of discussions between the two INDIA bloc allies on the assembly polls, which are expected to take place in February-March next year, according to the report.Last week, SP president and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Akhilesh Yadav claimed that the Congress had demanded 181 seats. However, the SP is expected to make an initial offer of just 24 seats to the Congress.Meanwhile, the Akhilesh Yadav-led party announced on Sunday that a four-member panel will hold seat-sharing talks with the Congress. The committee will include Rajya Sabha MP and Akhilesh Yadav's uncle Ram Gopal Yadav, Uttar Pradesh unit president Shyamlal Pal, and Lok Sabha MPs Rajeev Rai and Iqra Hasan.The SP is eyeing a comeback in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections after suffering back-to-back defeats in 2017 and 2022. In 2017, when Akhilesh Yadav was the chief minister, the SP and Congress contested as allies, winning 47 and seven seats, respectively.In 2022, the two parties fought separately, with the SP increasing its tally to 111 seats, while the Congress' tally shrunk to just two seats.The alliance, however, delivered a strong performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections under the INDIA bloc banner. The SP secured 37 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 parliamentary constituencies, while the Congress won six.Uttar Pradesh, with 403 assembly constituencies, is expected to see a keen contest between the BJP and the SP in 2027, as the saffron party seeks a third consecutive term in office.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Black Friday is always the day after Thanksgiving, and this year, it falls on Friday, Nov. 27. That said, many retailers kick off their Black Friday sales earlier, which is why this month is often referred to as "Black November." Yes, this means you'll be bombarded with holiday sale messaging long before your turkey has even defrosted, but the good news is, you'll be able to get a head start on your gift shopping ahead of the Black Friday hubbub.

What is the difference between Black Friday and Cyber Monday?

Black Friday sales usually continue through the holiday weekend and into Cyber Monday, which is on Monday, Nov. 30. While the two savings events have merged into one long weekend of markdowns for the most part, Black Friday sales often involve a mix of in-store and online discounts, whereas Cyber Monday has historically been a web-focused sale extravaganza.

Deals will vary from retailer to retailer, so just because you see something on sale during Black Friday, don't assume it'll still be discounted for Cyber Monday. When in doubt, add to cart and check out!

During sales like Prime Day , we usually advise readers to hold off on purchasing items in the tech and large appliance categories — and that's because it's worth waiting until Black Friday. If you've wanted to upgrade your TV or get a new dishwasher, this is the time to do it!

To be honest, there's not much we wouldn't recommend buying during Black Friday; most major retailers will be offering some of their deepest discounts of the year on everything from kitchen essentials to beauty favorites, and it's also a stellar time to stock up on clothing. Of course, many of us will be shopping for gifts, so if you see something on your list for a great price, grab it before it sells out.

The only things you should steer clear of? Bad deals. Not all Black Friday sales are created equal, so it's important to pick out the legit markdowns from the duds. Retailers can sneakily raise starting prices to make a discount seem more impressive than it is, and it's always a good idea to compare sales across the web to make sure you're getting the best price. articles.title: Wildfowl deaths prompts fishing tackle warning in Cornwall
articles.summary: Cornwall Council said there were 15 cases of wildfowl injury and 3 deaths linked to discarded items.
articles.body:
Anglers are being urged to "fish responsibly" to protect wildlife after geese and swans were killed by discarded tackle.

Cornwall Council said abandoned lines, hooks and lures had been linked to 15 cases of wildfowl injury and three deaths over the past few months at St Andrew's Wetland Nature Reserve in Par, Cornwall.

It said one Canada goose was found in distress with a lure and attached line wrapped around its legs and later died.

Loic Rich, cabinet member for environment on Cornwall Council, said the birds had been through some "quite horrific experiences, experiencing a lot of pain and suffering" and warned that if things did not change they would ban fishing at the site.

The council said about 30 items of angling equipment, most designed for pike fishing, were recovered from the pond and surrounding vegetation - with some of the equipment illegal on inland waters.

Rich said it was "a really special place for wildlife" and fishing had taken place there for a very long time.

He said while the vast majority of the anglers were responsible, some people were not.

"There's no excuse, there's no justification for leaving lines behind - it really doesn't take much effort to ensure that you don't leave anything behind that you shouldn't."

"The animals are not like we are as humans. If they get wrapped up in these lines, it is awful for them, quite frankly," Rich said.

"They panic, they don't know what's going on.

"It's just not acceptable to allow animals to suffer like that, so if we can't encourage people to fish responsibly, we'll ban it, and it will be policed as well."

"The priority is the safety of the wildlife - wildlife has to come first."

Rich said the council did "not want to come down heavy-handed for no reason" but was committed to educating people to prevent the "awful injuries".

He said more signs and a code of conduct would be installed to "make it much clearer, but it should be common sense, you don't leave dangerous things that are a danger to wildlife out in the wild".

The council said Environment Agency officers would patrol the site to check people were following national and local by-laws and had a valid rod licence.

articles.title: A New York inn faced a lawsuit after a patron alleged injuries on its premises, but its insurer refused to defend it by citing an assault exclusion; an appeals court ordered the company to pay for the inn's legal defence
articles.summary: A New York appeals court has ruled that an insurance company must defend a bar owner in a customer's personal injury lawsuit and pay the legal fees,
articles.body: A New York appeals court has ruled that an insurance company must defend a bar owner in a customer's personal injury lawsuit and pay the legal fees, rejecting the insurer's attempt to deny coverage under an assault and battery exclusion.The Appellate Division, Fourth Department, issued the ruling on November 20 in a case involving Ratava LLC, which operates the Tow Bar Inn, and Utica First Insurance Company.The dispute began after a patron filed a personal injury lawsuit against the bar, alleging that she was injured because of the establishment's negligence. The complaint accused the business of failing to properly maintain its premises and included negligence claims but did not mention an altercation.Utica First Insurance had refused to provide coverage, citing an assault and battery exclusion in the commercial Businessowners Policy it had issued to the bar. The insurer argued that its own investigation showed the patron's injuries resulted from an altercation on the premises.Ratava subsequently filed a lawsuit seeking a declaration that the insurer was required to defend it and provide coverage in the underlying personal injury case.A lower court had allowed the insurer to seek additional evidence through discovery and denied the bar owner's request for partial summary judgment. Ratava challenged that decision before the appeals court.Court says insurer must defend bar ownerThe appeals court ruled that the insurer could not rely on its own investigation to avoid its duty to defend the business when the underlying complaint alleged negligence that potentially fell within the policy's coverage.The judges emphasised that an insurer's duty to defend is broad and applies whenever the allegations in a lawsuit suggest a reasonable possibility of coverage.They also said an insurance company seeking to rely on a policy exclusion must demonstrate that the allegations fall entirely within that exclusion, leaving no reasonable possibility of coverage.In this case, the judges found that the underlying complaint concerned premises liability and alleged negligent maintenance of the bar's property, claims that could be covered under the insurance policy.The court also rejected the insurer's argument that further discovery was necessary, explaining that the duty to defend had to be determined by examining the allegations within the four corners of the underlying complaint.Bar owner allowed to choose its own lawyerThe appeals court further ruled that Ratava was entitled to hire an attorney of its choice because the insurer's interests conflicted with those of the business.It directed Utica First to pay the reasonable and necessary legal fees of the bar owner's chosen lawyer, along with related costs incurred in defending the personal injury lawsuit.The court modified the lower court's order to grant Ratava partial summary judgment on its right to a legal defence and independent counsel. The remaining portions of the lower court's order were affirmed.The ruling means the insurer must fund the bar owner's legal defence even as the underlying personal injury dispute continues.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jharkhand sees rural-urban gap in adolescent pregnancy indicators
articles.summary: NFHS-6 shows Jharkhand’s adolescent pregnancy rose to 11.7% (13.3% rural, 4.7% urban) even as child marriage fell; dropouts, migration cited.
articles.body: Jharkhand has reported a troubling rise in adolescent pregnancies even as fewer women report being married before 18. The figures, according to the National Family Health Survey-6, highlight gaps between policy progress and lived realities, particularly in rural communities, where weak school retention, forced migration and limited access to adolescent health services continue to affect girls.Widening rural gapNearly one in nine girls aged 15 to 19 years in Jharkhand is already a mother or pregnant, according to NFHS-6, released earlier this year. The proportion stands at 11.7%, above the national average of 6.7%. Jharkhand is among the states with the highest adolescent childbearing rates, after Tripura (18%) and West Bengal (16.6%), and ahead of Bihar (11.4%).The situation has worsened since NFHS-5, which recorded the figure at 9.8% — a rise of 1.9 percentage points.The rural-urban divide is stark. Rural areas recorded an adolescent childbearing rate of 13.3%, compared with 4.7% in urban areas. The rural rate is nearly three times the urban figure, pointing to disparities in education, healthcare access and social conditions.The pattern is similar in child marriage. The proportion of women aged 20-24 who were married before 18 declined from 32.2% in NFHS-5 to 28.1% in NFHS-6. However, the improvement has not translated into a corresponding decline in adolescent pregnancies. In urban areas, 11.1% of women were married before the legal age, against 32.2% in rural Jharkhand.Child rights activists said the causes are interconnected. School dropouts, migration for work, social norms in some tribal communities and child marriage are leaving adolescents vulnerable to early pregnancies, exploitation and abuse.Tanvi Jha, state head of the Child In Need Institute, said early partner selection in some tribal communities and limited communication between parents and children were contributing to the problem.“Large family sizes in some tribal communities often mean adolescents do not receive adequate care and guidance. Teenagers sometimes drift away from their aspirations and prioritise relationships over education and careers. While some communities are relatively open and live-in relationships are accepted in sections of society, conversations around reproductive health and the right age to make important life decisions remain inadequate,” Jha said.Sanjay Mishra, founder of Bal Kalyan Sangh and a former member of the Jharkhand State Commission for Protection of Child Rights, said lack of jobs and rising school dropouts were pushing adolescents to migrate, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.“Many girls who leave school migrate to other states in search of work. Middlemen lure them with false promises of employment and take them to other parts of the country, where they may face sexual exploitation, sometimes resulting in pregnancy. In several cases, the girls are unaware that they are pregnant,” Mishra said.UDISE+ 2025-26 data show that dropouts rose across school stages: from zero to 0.1% at the primary level, 1.7% to 2.5% at the upper-primary level, and 3.5% in 2024-25 to 6.6% in 2025-26 at the secondary level.Peer powerRafat Farzana, state coordinator for adolescent health at Jharkhand chapter of the National Health Mission, said a multi-department study was needed to identify the factors driving teenage pregnancy.Under the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram, the health department has identified adolescent peer educators in villages across 12 districts.Four peer educators are selected for every 1,000 adolescents in Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega, Seraikela-Kharsawan, West Singhbhum, Hazaribag, Sahibganj, Khunti, Dumka, Ranchi, Jamtara and Bokaro.Selected by village-level committees, they undergo six days of training before spreading awareness on sexual and reproductive health, substance abuse, mental health, non-communicable diseases and other adolescent concerns.Farzana said the programme had helped the educators become role models and encouraged other teenagers to pursue a better future. Several peer educators, she said, had stopped their own marriages and intervened to prevent child marriages among peers.Rakesh Senger, programme head of the Kailash Satyarthi Children’s Foundation, said the govt needed to examine the links between school dropouts, migration and early pregnancy. The foundation, he said, had helped free more than 600 villages in Koderma and Giridih from child labour and child marriage, turning them into “child-friendly villages”.In these villages, councils of children, youth and women monitor girls’ safety. Children from economically weaker families receive school supplies and fee support. Such interventions, activists said, can help keep adolescents in school and prevent early parenthood.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: 'Failed to communicate double-engine govt's work': Union minister on BJP's poor show in Rajasthan panchayat polls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union minister and BJP leader Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Sunday blamed the party's poor performance in the Rajasthan Zilla Parishad and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister and BJP leader Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Sunday blamed the party's poor performance in the Rajasthan Zilla Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections on what he described as its "failure" to take the work of the "double-engine government" to the people at the grassroots level."Somewhere along the way, we failed to properly inform people at the grassroots level about the work done by the double-engine government. Our workers may also have lacked enthusiasm and energy on some issues," he told reporters in Jaipur.The term "double-engine government", coined by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, refers to a situation where the BJP is in power both at the Centre and in a state.Meanwhile, Shekhawat added that the BJP has started reviewing its election performance, following its usual practice of analysing both wins and losses."The BJP has a practice of conducting reviews after every victory and every defeat. Whether we win or lose an election, we sit down and review our performance. The review process has now begun at various levels within the party. Reviews will take place at the grassroots, district and constituency levels, and later in Jaipur as well," he added.The Congress registered a strong victory in the Zilla Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections in Rajasthan, where the BJP is in power.Of the 37 Zilla Parishads, the Congress secured a majority in 27 districts, including in capital Jaipur, as well as in Jodhpur and Bikaner. The BJP managed to win a majority in only six districts, while the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) secured a majority in Nagaur.In the elections to 419 Panchayat Samitis across 37 districts, the Congress won 269, while the BJP secured 73. Other parties and independent candidates won 60 Panchayat Samitis. No party could secure a clear majority in the remaining 17.Counting in Kota, Sri Ganganagar, Baran and Karauli districts is scheduled for December 17.The results are being viewed as an indication of the political mood in Rajasthan, where the BJP and Congress have alternated in power after single terms in recent years. The next Rajasthan assembly elections are scheduled for December 2028.(With ANI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: JHAJJAR: BJP national general secretary and Haryana in-charge Smriti Irani, accompanied by party national secretary and state co-in-charge Dr Bhola Singh, will undertake a three-day organisational tour of Haryana from December 4 to 6, visiting Jind, Rohtak and Jhajjar.The visit is aimed at strengthening the party organisation through direct interaction with leaders and workers across different levels, including senior party veterans, district office-bearers, former public representatives and grassroots functionaries.The party has drawn up an extensive itinerary covering a series of meetings in all three districts. The programme will provide an opportunity for the visiting leaders to interact with both experienced organisational functionaries and newer workers, while reviewing the party's organisational network at the district and booth levels.Former Haryana agriculture minister Om Prakash Dhankar said the party was making elaborate preparations for the visit. He said Irani's proposed visit to Jhajjar was particularly significant as it would be her first visit to the district.Several organisational meetings have been planned at the BJP office, including interactions with former office-bearers who have served three terms, former state-level office-bearers residing in the district and former office-bearers of various party wings.The three-day tour will begin in Jind on December 4. Irani and Singh are scheduled to meet senior party workers aged above 70 between noon and 12.40 pm.This will be followed by interactions with district office-bearers, office secretaries, state-level functionaries residing in the district and presidents of various party wings.After lunch, the leaders will meet former office-bearers who have served three terms, former state-level functionaries and former office-bearers of party wings. A separate session has been scheduled with former public representatives who have served three terms.The evening schedule includes meetings with the minister in charge, district president, district in-charge and district general secretary, followed by a core group meeting from 6 pm to 7 pm.
